description: Variation of condition 03 of Ref:  24/04181/FUL to allow an increase to 3-6 staff members.
decision_conditions: The development to which this permission relates must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of the decision notice under 24/04181/FUL dated 11.02.2025. Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the approvedplans as set out in the attached schedule which forms part of this notice.Location Plan; Block Plan; Planning Statement; Cycle storage provision; 1.0 Rev 00; 1.1 Rev 00; (received 11 Dec 2024)Highway Impact Assessment (Received 16 Dec 2024)Planning Statement (received 10.03.2026)Reason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

REPLACEMENT CONDITION 3The development hereby permitted shall be occupied by no more than 4 residents and 6 members of staff (excluding ad hoc visiting specialists/ therapists) at any one time. Staffing levels at the premises shall be determined by the care, supervision and safeguarding needs of the residents.Reason: To minimize the impact of the development on the occupiers of neighbouring properties and to ensure that car parking provision complies with the Council's adopted standards.

Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes Order) 1 September 2020 (as Amended), the development shall only be used as a children's care home within Use Class C2 and for no other purpose whatsoever without express planning permission first being obtained from the Local Authority.Reason: In the interests of residential amenity, car parking and highway safety.

Prior to occupation, unless otherwise agreed cycle parking should be provided in compliancewith the following criteria:oProvision of a minimum of TWO long stay cycle parking spaceso in an accessible location: the access route to the store should be a minimum of 1.2m wide to enable the bike to enter the store, should be step free, close to the entrance and involve no more than 2 doors or gates (excluding the store door) which must also have a minimum opening width of 1.2mo secured: with a British Standard mortice lock or access fobo fully enclosed: 4 walls and a roofReason: The Council's Climate Action and Transport Policies seek to increase the use of active and sustainable transport modes. This means that access to bicycle parking should be easy and secure to remove potential barriers to cycling.

Prior to first occupation, details of the design of refuse storage facilities including facilities for the recycling of waste to satisfy the future number of occupiers on site, shall be provided within the development, in accordance with the London Borough of Enfield - Household Recycling and Waste Planning Guidance for New Developments (February 2024).In particular, waste collection vehicles must be able to get within 25m of the refuse storage point. Residents should not have to carry waste further than 30m.Reason: In order to facilitate efficient, safe and clean removal of household refuse, the location and accessibility of refuse storage plus to maintain safety on the Highway.
